content: Patients with a documented allergy to spectinomycin or beta-lactam antibiotics were excluded from certain studies. Microbiological cure rates were assessed in various trials, with ceftriaxone 250 mg administered intramuscularly as a single dose being a common treatment. For example, in a study conducted by Mroczkowski in 1997 in the USA, adolescent and adult women aged 15–54 years with uncomplicated cervical, rectal, or pharyngeal gonorrhea were included. These women either had Gram-stained endocervical smears showing gram-negative intracellular diplococci (GNID) within polymorphonuclear leukocytes, a recent untreated culture positive for Neisseria gonorrhoeae (NG), or sexual exposure to men with urethral gonorrhea within two weeks prior to enrollment. Women with concomitant infections, complicated gonococcal infections, pregnancy, nursing, hypersensitivity to quinolone or cephalosporin antibiotics, recent antibiotic use, or other conditions compromising treatment evaluation were excluded. In another study by Pabst in 1989 in the USA, adolescent and adult women aged 16 years and older with urogenital gonorrhea were treated with ceftriaxone 1 g intramuscularly as a single dose. Inclusion criteria were similar, involving Gram-stained endocervical smears showing GNID or recent untreated culture positivity for NG. Exclusion criteria included penicillin or quinolone allergy, complicated gonococcal infections, untreated syphilis, recent antimicrobial therapy effective against NG, or failure to attend follow-up visits. A study by Panikabutra in 1985 in Thailand focused on men with uncomplicated gonococcal urethritis diagnosed by Gram-stained smear microscopy. Ceftriaxone 250 mg intramuscularly was used, and microbiological cure rates and adverse events were reported. Similarly, Plourde's 1992 study in Kenya included men and women aged 18–65 years with uncomplicated urethral and cervical gonorrhea. Patients with complicated infections, hypersensitivity to penicillins or cephalosporins, other sexually transmitted infections (STIs), or pregnancy were excluded. Portilla's 1992 study in the USA included men and women aged 18–44 years with uncomplicated urethritis or cervicitis. Patients with GNID consistent with NG were treated with ceftriaxone 250 mg intramuscularly or cefixime 400 mg orally as a single dose. Exclusion criteria included penicillin or cephalosporin allergy, chronic bowel disorders, multiple bacterial infections, evidence of chancroid, syphilis, or AIDS, severe systemic diseases, or pregnancy. Romapalo's 1994 study in the USA included men and women aged 15–60 years with uncomplicated urethral, cervical, pharyngeal, or rectal gonorrhea. Patients with Gram-stained smears showing GNID or recent sexual exposure to a partner with gonorrhea were included. Exclusion criteria involved disseminated gonorrhea, pelvic inflammatory disease (PID), septic arthritis, recent antibiotic therapy, active kidney or liver disease, bleeding disorders, or negative cultures for NG at enrollment. Schumacher's 2013 study in the USA included men and women with genital and extragenital gonorrhea, with a median age of 24 years. Patients were treated with ceftriaxone 250 mg intramuscularly plus azithromycin 1 g orally as a single dose. Microbiological cure rates were reported. Shams-ur-Rahman's 2009 study in Saudi Arabia included men and women aged 14–55 years with urethral or cervical gonorrhea. Patients were treated with ceftriaxone 500 mg intramuscularly or spectinomycin 2 g intramuscularly as a single dose. Exclusion criteria included complicated infections, hypersensitivity to quinolones, impaired kidney or liver function, blood disorders, or coexistent syphilis. Other studies, such as those by Brown (1974), Cheng (2001), Davidson (1986), and Duncan (1972), evaluated spectinomycin as a treatment for gonorrhea. These studies included patients with uncomplicated gonococcal infections and excluded those with complicated infections, recent antibiotic use, or hypersensitivity to beta-lactam antibiotics. Microbiological cure rates and adverse events were reported. Overall, these studies highlight the efficacy of ceftriaxone and spectinomycin in treating uncomplicated gonorrhea, with specific inclusion and exclusion criteria ensuring the safety and reliability of the results.
